title: Dyninst on the RISC-V: Binary Instrumentation in Support of Performance, Debugging, and Other Tools
problem: Binary instrumentation tools like Dyninst are not yet available for the RISC-V architecture, limiting the ability to profile, debug, and analyze programs on RISC-V systems without access to source code.
motivation: RISC-V is an emerging open-source ISA gaining adoption in HPC and research systems. Existing tools support x86, ARM, and Power, but porting to RISC-V presents unique challenges. Tools enabling performance profiling, debugging, and tracing are critical for HPC systems.
method: Port the Dyninst binary instrumentation toolkit to the RISC-V architecture, addressing RISC-V-specific challenges in binary parsing, instruction manipulation, and relocation handling.
key_novelty: First port of Dyninst to RISC-V, demonstrating that the instrumentation framework can be extended to new ISAs while preserving the unified tool ecosystem approach.
contributions: Documentation of RISC-V-specific challenges (instruction encoding, relocations, ABI conventions)
Integration with existing Dyninst ecosystem for binary analysis and instrumentation
limitations: Paper is abstract-only; specific performance and completeness metrics not available.
